findings.text: Wakeup placement hook selects a destination CPU for a fair task from previous CPU, wake flags and topology. It records wakees, offers a fast return on current CPU, attempts an energy aware choice when the root domain is not overutilized, evaluates affine candidacy, walks scheduling domains for affine and balance flags, then uses a slow balance path when a domain matches or an idle sibling choice on the wakeup path.

Energy candidate replaces the prior target when its fit score is strictly greater, or when both are usable and its energy delta is smaller, or when both are unusable and its actual capacity is larger. Otherwise the previous target is retained.

Performance domain span has two build variants: one exposes the CPU set of the associated energy model, the other reports absence with a null value. Callers must handle the null case as no energy model.

Cross runqueue migration detaches load average when the task is not already marked migrating, compensates estimated lag for PELT continuity, clears the last update timestamp to signal migration, and refreshes the NUMA scan period. Task exit only detaches load average.

Maximum allowed capacity is inactive unless asymmetric capacity is enabled. When active it is set to the capacity of the first RCU list entry whose span intersects task affinity, and it is refreshed whenever fair affinity is changed.

Wakeup preemption uses four outcomes: none means keep current, short means ignore slice protection, pick means defer to eligibility selection, resched means force rescheduling. Buddy helpers retain an existing next buddy when it is earlier or shorter, otherwise nominate the wakee.

Synchronous wakeup preemption compares elapsed runtime since current execution start against a migration cost threshold, reduced when tasks stack on one CPU. It permits rescheduling only when the wakee precedes current in deadline order and the threshold has elapsed. Negative elapsed time is clamped to zero.

Fair wakeup preemption applies only between fair entities that are distinct and unthrottled, subject to feature gates and an existing reschedule request. It prefers non idle over idle, refreshes current state, excludes non normal policies, delayed tasks and fork wakeups from preemption, allows a short slice override, nominates a next buddy, selects among none, forced and pick actions, and manages slice protection before requesting rescheduling.
Deadline server pick for fair requires the runqueue lock of the queue owning the deadline entity to be held by the caller.

Putting the previous fair task walks up the entity hierarchy, putting each level unless the next task shares the group, then clears the root current pointer and requeues the previous entity when still on the runqueue. A warning guards an unexpected root current.

Fair yield is a no operation with a single runnable task. Otherwise it clears buddies, updates clock and current statistics while skipping a microscopic update, and forfeits remaining virtual time to the deadline only when eligible. Yield to another task succeeds only when the target is queued and not delayed, nominates it as next buddy, then yields the caller.

Load balance environment carries domain, source and destination CPUs and queues, destination core idle state, destination group mask, revised destination, idle kind, imbalance amount, candidate CPU set, flags, loop counters and limits, queue scan scope, migration reason, and a task list.

Scheduler group classification has eight states: spare capacity, fully busy, misfit task needing a stronger CPU, SMT balance opportunity, asymmetric packing preference, affinity induced imbalance, LLC preference balance, and overload. LLC balance ranks below overload and above the remaining states, with failed attempts falling back through the failure counter.
Load balance flag values are distinct bits: all pinned is 1, need break is 2, destination pinned is 4, some pinned is 8, active balance is 16, LLC pinned is 32, active LLC balance is 64.

Group statistics aggregate average and total load, capacity, utilization, runnable time, total and fair running counts, idle CPU count, weight, group type, packing and SMT and LLC movement hints, misfit load, and overutilization, with optional NUMA and cache preference counters. Domain statistics hold busiest and local groups, total load and capacity, average load, sibling preference, and both group statistic blocks.

Migration reasons are load, utilization, task count, misfit, and LLC task. Queue scan scopes are regular, remote, and all. LLC migration permission has three values: forbid and respect preference, allow LLC preference migration, and unrestricted generic migration.

Detaching a single task requires the source runqueue lock held. The operation scans the source fair tasks in reverse, detaches the first task allowed to migrate, and accounts a gained balance event for the current idle level.
Blocked average update for one CPU takes that runqueue lock with interrupts saved through a scoped guard, updates the runqueue clock, then updates blocked averages.

Active balancing runs as a stopper on the busiest CPU. It rejects inactive CPUs, wrong CPU or cleared request, and single runnable queues, warns when source equals target, finds a domain spanning both CPUs under RCU, detaches one task with active flags, resets the domain failure counter on success, clears the request, attaches the task on the target, and reenables interrupts. Plain and LLC entry points differ only by the extra LLC flag.

Periodic domain balancing walks domains under RCU, decays new idle costs and accumulates maximum cost, stops descending when another CPU in the group balances more actively, balances expired domains and refreshes idle state and timestamps, tracks the earliest next balance time, maintains a runqueue idle cost floor, and publishes the next balance deadline when any domain was visited.

Idle transition for a CPU marks its last level cache domain as nohz idle exactly once when the domain is shared, and decrements the shared busy CPU count. Absent, unshared, or already idle domains cause no change.
Maximum pinned interval is 512. Default maximum load balance interval is one tenth of a second. The count of balancing runners is an atomic starting at zero.
Placement requires the task pi lock held for stable affinity. Asymmetric list traversal, active domain search, periodic balancing, and idle state lookup execute inside RCU read side sections.

Active balancing has a window between queuing and execution where CPUs may go inactive, so liveness must be rechecked under lock before moving a task. A same queue source and target is treated as impossible and warned about.
